records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Introduction to the Administration of Criminal Justice
records.description: Agencies and processes in the administration of criminal justice.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Introduction to Criminological Theory
records.description: Analysis of conceptions of crime and seriousness as determined by societal factors.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Advancing Justice: Addressing Power and Inequity in the Justice System
records.description: The pursuit of justice and the historical, contemporary, and future issues and challenges facing society and the criminal justice system.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Research Methods for Criminal Justice
records.description: Discussion of research methods appropriate for the study of crime and criminal justice policies and institutions.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Criminal Law
records.description: Substantive criminal law; principles, functions, and limits; basic crime categories, state and national legal research materials.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Quantitative Methods for Criminal Justice
records.description: Critical discussion of skills and methods needed for the analysis of implementation and impact of criminal justice policies.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Crime Control Policies
records.description: Analysis of ideologies, assumptions, and performance of crime control policies.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Juvenile Justice and Corrections
records.description: History, philosophy, legal process, performance, and outcomes of the juvenile justice and corrections systems. (Crosslisted course offered as CRM J 365, SOC 367.)

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Policing and Society
records.description: Development, organization, policies, and performance of the police.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Criminal Courts in America
records.description: Structure and process of the prosecution and adjudication of individuals charged with crimes in the criminal court system.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Crime and Justice in the Movies
records.description: Mass media as both reflector and shaper of public attitudes and opinions about crime, criminals, law, order, and justice; using films. (Crosslisted course offered as CRM J 381, POL S 381.)

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Institutional Corrections
records.description: Ideologies of punishment and correction, intermediary sanctioning and reintegration policies in the criminal justice system.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Criminal Justice Management
records.description: Predominate and progressive thought and theory of criminal justice administration in the U.S.; exploring important and troubling issues faced by those involved in managing criminal justice agencies.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Special Topics in Criminal Justice and Criminology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: CRM J 101; junior standing.

records.title: Violence Toward Women

records.title: Comparative Criminal Justice Systems

records.description: Principal court decisions concerning standards of conduct and rights in the criminal process.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Community Corrections
records.description: Theory practice and human impact of treating criminal offenders in the community.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Victimology and Public Policy
records.description: Examination of victimization; policy responses to victims; victim's rights.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Crime Prevention Strategies

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Drug and Alcohol Use and Abuse
records.description: Drug use, impact on behavior and drug control policies.

records.title: Senior Seminar: Ethical Issues in Criminal Justice

records.title: Addictive Behavior Among Diverse Populations

records.title: Senior Capstone in Criminal Justice and Criminology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: CRM J 101; CRM J 311; CRM J 321; senior standing.
records.description: Experiential learning emphasizing refining skills and preparing students for the myriad of challenges awaiting them in public safety.

records.title: Criminal Justice Internship
records.description: On/off-campus internship in criminal justice institutions (police, FBI, jails, law firms, etc.); written assignments and readings will be required.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Special Topics: Study Abroad
records.description: Criminal Justice Study Abroad.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: The Complex Social Interaction Bodycam Research Lab
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: By instructor permission; CRM J 101.
records.description: Experimental research conducted under the jurisdiction of an approving faculty member; may include analysis of individual, situational, and environmental factors on police interactions, examination of the influence of various contextual factors on community policing dynamics, and critical examination of police decision-making and accountability in complex social interactions.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: CRM_J
records.title: Special Problems
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite:  By Instructor permission; CRM J 101.
records.description: Independent study conducted under the jurisdiction of an approving faculty member; may include independent research studies in technical or specialized problems; selection and analysis of specified readings; development of a creative project; or field experiences.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.
